messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing a cluster of tiny GPU pods stuck Pending in ap-southeast1. Not normal fragmentation; scheduler prebinds are failing with 'no slot after reservation'. Anyone else?
raj: yup saw similar in eu-west1 this morning but assumed a warmpool hiccup.
nana: (typo) meant ana: can you paste the scheduler logs?
maya: paste below — this repeats on every prebind attempt:```scheduler: prebind failed for pod gpu-tiny-xyz; reason=prebind_error: reservation allocated but no matching slot found after reservation check; node=gpupool-warmpool-027; pool=small-1```
nana: (ana) ok thanks. that looks like the late-prebind optimization race we rolled last week.
tony: quick `kubectl` snapshot:```$ kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | grep Pending
gpu-tiny-xyz   0/1     Pending   0          2m
gpu-tiny-abc   0/1     Pending   0          5m
gpu-batch-12   0/1     Pending   0          10m
```
infra-bot: Autoscaler: scaled up nodepool ap-se1-warmpool by 2 nodes at 2025-06-03T14:17:03Z (reason: pending pods > threshold).
raj: autoscaler added capacity but scheduler still can't bind — suggests reservation -> bind mismatch. Could be slot metadata drift (labels/taints) between reservation and final bind.
nana: (ana) any recent taint rollout? we pushed `gpu:dedicated=true:NoSchedule` earlier but that should be fine.
maya: I dug into scheduler state — reservations created with nodeSelector `gpu.class: small-v2` but nodes got relabeled to `gpu.class: small-v2a` during a nodepool image update. prebind finds the reservation but final check rejects.
raj: oh nice catch. node relabels during rolling upgrade. reservation doesn't reconcile label rename. that explains why eu-west saw similar when we upgraded small-v2 -> small-v2a.
tony: Proposed mitigation: make prebind check tolerate equivalent label aliases for 10m, or disable prebind optimization until we reconcile labels. Quickest is to patch scheduler config to skip the final strict label-check for reservations.
nana: (ana) downside: could place pods on slightly different gpu class and risk perf variation. but better than P95 pending times.
maya: plan: canary patch scheduler in ap-southeast1 to disable strict prebind final-check for 5 minutes, monitor scheduling rate and perf. if good, roll to other regions. I'll prepare the kubeconfig patch.
raj: I'll standby to revert if we see noisy evictions. also let's emit an event metric `prebind_alias_bypass` when we allow alias match so we can track.
nana: runbook note: if we see >10% of pods scheduled onto different gpu.class than requested, revert immediately and set back to strict.
maya: applying canary now: `kubectl -n infra patch configmaps/scheduler-config -p '{"data":{"prebindStrict": "false"}}'`
infra-bot: Deploy: scheduler canary ap-se1 started (revision v2025.6.3-canary-2) by maya at 2025-06-03T14:19:18Z
tony: can you tail the scheduler log for prebind_alias_bypass metric?
maya: tailing logs:```I0603 14:19:25 scheduler.go: prebind_alias_bypass: pod=gpu-tiny-xyz reservation=rs-442 -> allowed alias match``````
maya: after patch, initial batch: 3/9 Pending pods transitioned to Running in ~40s. looks promising.
raj: great. can you keep canary for 15m and then roll? I'll open a PR to add alias mapping for label renames so this is permanent and explicit.
nana: also add a telemetry comment in the release notes — this behavior can bite upgrades.
maya: will do. pinging oncall+infra for awareness. thx all :thumbsup:
